_comment: Domain registry for FLEET_SELFREPAIR_DESIGN.md §3/§4.1. A domain names a path scope (prefixes/globs within hermes-self-repair-read.py's own allowlist.json, never outside it -- see that file's header for why the allowlist lives in the tool's own installation, not the target checkout), a detection source, a completeness rule, a cadence, and its own self-managed-mode switch, independent of every other domain. Read by tools/hermes_self_repair_domains.py (underscore-named -- importable, unlike every hyphenated *.py in tools/); nothing else parses this file directly. Domain #1 (minecraft-bots) was added here in Phase 3 (§8.3), after the completeness hook (§4.3, tools/hermes_self_repair_completeness.py) and detection bridge (§4.4, tools/hermes-self-repair-bridge.py) it depends on were both built and offline-tested. self_managed started false (§3's own table: 'Off by default, scoped to this domain only') and was flipped to true by direct operator instruction (2026-11-08, after Phase 3's own offline verification and two real gaps -- the backlog-replay risk and the missing per-cycle submission cap -- were found and fixed in the bridge, 1.1.0) -- this is what actually lets the detection bridge auto-submit real tasks from live triage incidents. Domain #2 (egress-guard) was added in Phase 4 (§8.4) as the genericity acceptance check's own real second domain -- deliberately left switched off, since this registration exists to prove the mechanism generalizes, not to start auto-submitting fixes against a security control. Its path_scope is deliberately EMPTY: unlike minecraft-bots, egress-guard's 'domain' is about the SOURCE of detection (a denial), not a bounded set of files it owns -- the fix target is whatever CALLER triggered the denial, which could be any allowlisted file in the fleet. An empty path_scope means domain_for_path() never attributes a file to egress-guard (deliberate, per that function's own docstring: an unscoped domain matches nothing rather than silently claiming everything) -- anything that looks up a task's domain by its target path (the FleetOps UI's domain column/filter, §4.8; the registered-PR mechanism's own branch naming, §4.6) will label these tasks/branches 'unregistered' despite coming from a registered, named source. This is a real, accepted limitation of the current path_scope-as-ownership model for a detection-source-shaped domain, not a bug: fixing it would mean touching hermes-fleetops-ui.py's or hermes-self-repair-open-pr.py's own domain-labeling logic, which this acceptance check exists specifically to avoid needing.
